Code that contacts it can be the last step of an SSRF; the same literal is also how an SSRF defence names what it blocks, and a pattern cannot tell the two apart, so this is listed for review and not deducted.

evidence.label: mcp-js-sql-string-built (medium/low)
evidence.detail: Listed, not deducted: this check is new and its precision has not been measured, so it is shown for review and scores nothing. A SQL statement is assembled by string building — a template literal that interpolates, or concatenation with something that is not a constant — and passed straight to a query method. A value built in can always be sent as a query parameter instead (pg's `/** `, mysql2's and sqlite's `?`, a tagged `sql` template), and a caller-supplied one is SQL injection; an identifier (a table or column name) cannot be a parameter and must be validated or quoted. This check cannot tell which the built part is, so it is listed for review, not deducted.
